newsitem.title: UK: Hundreds may die from mad cow link-scientists.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds may die from mad cow link-scientists.

text.p: Hundreds of Britons will die every year from the brain disease that may be linked to mad cow disease, government scientists monitoring its progress were quoted as saying on Tuesday.
Scientists said the number of deaths could peak in about seven years' time.

The European Union imposed a ban on British beef after scientists disclosed in March a probable link between mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), and the invariably fatal Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD), which rots human brains.
The latest mortality predictions, cited by the Independent newspaper, were made by the CJD Surveillance Unit in Edinburgh.

Dr James Ironside, co-author of a paper giving the estimates, told Tuesday's Independent: "Thankfully this is not the doomsday scenario that some have predicted where the British population is decimated. That doesn't seem to be on the cards.
"It looks as though the total number of cases over the whole course of the disease will be in hundreds, rather than thousands."
The symptoms of CJD -- depression, failing co-ordination, dementia and coma leading to death -- take up to two years to develop. The incubation period can be up to 15 years.
